articles.title: Alienware 16X Aurora review: A thoroughly competent gaming laptop
articles.text:
Tom's Hardware Verdict
The Alienware 16X Aurora is a capable, well-rounded gaming laptop with a standout OLED display, strong productivity performance, and good build quality, though its weight and middling battery life make it better suited to desk duty than daily travel.
Pros
- +Excellent 16-inch OLED display
- +Solid gaming and productivity performance
- +Sturdy, understated design
- +Broad port selection
- +Good upgrade prospects
Cons
- -Heavy, desktop-replacement feel
- -Middling battery life
- -Dim single-zone keyboard backlight
Why you can trust Tom's Hardware
Alienware’s 16X Aurora (starts at $1,979.99) isn’t just another spec-sheet powerhouse – it’s a statement in restraint. Alienware has shifted toward performance-first minimalism with a cleaner, RGB-free chassis, but it doesn’t compromise on the specs: a 16-inch OLED display running at a blistering 240 Hz, Intel’s Core Ultra HX-series CPU, and Nvidia’s latest RTX 50-series graphics. While its bulk and limited battery life prevents it from being a great travel companion, the Aurora’s overall competence make it worth your attention.
Design of the Alienware 16X Aurora
The Aurora is a discreet gaming laptop. Aside from its nearly inch-thick profile, it does little to distinguish itself. Alienware’s “interstellar indigo” chassis is plain, and the iconic Alien head on the lid is hard to see against it. Unlike many previous-generation Alienware laptops, this one has no external lighting.
Alienware’s build quality is substantial, with aluminum top and bottom panels. A magnesium internal frame keeps the laptop rigid, though the lid can still be opened one-handed. Rounded edges on the bottom of the chassis make the Aurora comfortable to transport, though at 5.66 pounds, it’s a handful. Acer’s Nitro V 16S AI (4.55 pounds) and Gigabyte’s Aero X16 (4.2 pounds) are much lighter.
Alienware’s port selection spreads across the left and rear edges: Thunderbolt 4, USB-C (10 Gbps), two USB-A (5 Gbps), HDMI 2.1, Ethernet, and an audio jack. Having some connections on the back, particularly the barrel-style power connector, preserves mouse space. Internally, the Aurora includes Wi-Fi 7 courtesy of a MediaTek MT7925 card.
Alienware 16X Aurora Specifications
| CPU | Intel Core Ultra 7 270HX Plus | 
| Graphics | Nvidia GeForce RTX 5060 (8GB GDDR7, 115 W, 1,455 MHz boost clock) | 
| Memory | 16GB DDR5-5600 (2x 8GB) | 
| Storage | 1TB PCIe 4.0 SSD (SanDisk SN7100S) | 
| Display | 16-inch, 2560 x 1600, OLED, 240 Hz, Nvidia G-Sync | 
| Networking | MediaTek Wi-Fi 7 MT7925, Bluetooth 6 | 
| Ports | 2x USB-A (5 Gbps), USB-C (10Gbps), Thunderbolt 4, HDMI 2.1, universal audio jack, Ethernet | 
| Camera | 1080p IR | 
| Battery | 96 Whr | 
| Power Adapter | 180 W (barrel connector) | 
| Operating System | Windows 11 Home | 
| Dimensions (WxDxH) | 14.05 x 10.45 x 0.92 inches (357 x 265 x 24 mm) | 
| Weight | 5.66 pounds (2.57 kg) | 
| Price (as configured) | $2,279.99 | 
Gaming and Graphics on the Alienware 16X Aurora
We tested the 16X Aurora in its entry-level configuration, featuring a Core Ultra 7 270HX Plus processor, a GeForce RTX 5060 GPU, and 16GB of dual-channel DDR5-5600 RAM.
I saw between 60 and 70 frames per second (fps) playing 007 First Light at 2560 x 1600 with medium settings and DLSS (but not frame generation). The game ran smoothly and didn’t stutter.
For performance comparisons, the Aurora faced the Acer Nitro V 16S AI (Ryzen 7 260, RTX 5060 85 W, $1,299.99 when tested), the Asus TUF Gaming F16 (Core i7-14650HX, RTX 5050 115 W, $1,199.99), and the Gigabyte Aero X16 (Ryzen AI 7 350, RTX 5070 85 W, $1,899.99).
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Our comparisons will focus on the 1920 x 1080 resolution. We also included results at each laptop's native resolution: 2560 x 1600 for our Aurora as well as the Gigabyte Aero X16, and 1920 x 1200 for the Acer Nitro and Asus TUF units.
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
The Aurora 16X is competitive but doesn't stand out in this group. In Shadow of the Tomb Raider, Far Cry 6, and Borderlands 3, it performed 20 to 25% better than the RTX 5060-powered Acer and RTX 5050-powered Asus, but those two surprisingly did better in Cyberpunk 2077 and matched the Aurora in Red Dead Redemption 2.
The Aurora produced varied results against the RTX 5070-powered Gigabyte; While the Aurora took a sizable lead in Far Cry 6 and matched it in Shadow of the Tomb Raider and Borderlands 3, it fell behind in Cyberpunk 2077 and Borderlands 3.
At its 2560 x 1600 native resolution, the Aurora took a drastic performance hit of around 50% from 1080p – from 111 to 64 fps in Shadow of the Tomb Raider, 101 to 72 fps in Far Cry 6, 99 to 64 fps in Borderlands 3, 28 to 15 fps in Cyberpunk 2077, and 69 to 45 fps in Red Dead Redemption 2 – but, excepting Cyberpunk 2077, its performance remained playable.
To stress-test gaming laptops, we run 15 loops of the Metro Exodus benchmark at RTX settings, simulating about half an hour of gaming. The Aurora averaged 76 fps across all runs with no more than a fraction of one frame between runs. During the test, the Core Ultra 7 270HX Plus ran at 3.1 GHz on its P-cores and 2.5 GHz on its E-cores while the RTX 5060 ran at 2.48 GHz.
Productivity Performance on the Alienware 16X Aurora
Our Aurora 16X arrives with a Core Ultra 7 270HX Plus, 16GB of RAM, and 1TB PCIe 4.0 SSD.
Powered by the Core Ultra 7 270HX Plus, the Aurora predictably outclassed these competitors, which all use previous-generation processors and/or lower-tier chips. In Geekbench 6, it took the top single-core (3,065) and multi-core (17,753) scores, distantly trailed by the Core i7-14650HX-powered Asus (2,710 and 15,013) and Ryzen AI 7 350-powered Gigabyte (2,916 and 14,074). It also clinched the leading time of 2 minutes and 25 seconds in our 4K-to-1080p Handbrake transcoding test, easily outdoing the Asus (3:33), Gigabyte (3:54), and Acer (4:32).
The Aurora also took top honors in our 25GB file transfer test, averaging 2,358.23 MBps. Acer’s Nitro V 16S AI (1,838.88 MBps), the next fastest unit, wasn’t even close.
Display on the Alienware 16X Aurora
All Aurora configurations include the same 16-inch OLED panel with a 2560 x 1600 resolution, 240 Hz refresh rate, and Nvidia G-Sync support. It’s the laptop’s standout feature, pairing the inky contrast expected from OLED with vivid color and unusually strong brightness for this panel type.
In 007 First Light, OLED added a level of depth that a lesser display wouldn’t match, giving shadow-heavy night scenes a richer, moodier look while keeping Malta’s sunlit desert environments bright and crisp. The panel’s sharpness and color also stood out while watching Avengers: Endgame, where fine details such as the nano-texture pattern on Iron Man’s suit were easy to pick out. There’s little to criticize here: the Aurora’s display is excellent.
Our lab results back that up. The Aurora peaked at 381.4 nits, which is bright for OLED and nearly tied the IPS-equipped Acer Nitro V 16S AI at 391.8 nits while nudging past the Gigabyte Aero X16’s 368.6 nits. Color coverage was also impressive, reaching 138% of DCI-P3 and topping both the Asus TUF Gaming F16 at 122.2% and the Gigabyte at 110.8%.
Keyboard and Touchpad on the Alienware 16X Aurora
I nearly matched my personal best typing speed on the 16X Aurora, hitting 123 words per minute with 99% accuracy in the MonkeyType typing test. The keys have enough travel and a precise feel, but the overall typing experience is competent rather than memorable. The RGB backlighting only has one zone, and while Alienware Command Center offers effects such as breathing, morph, pulse, spectrum, and rainbow wave, the excitement is undermined by the lighting being too dim to stand out in a well-lit room.
The touchpad is similarly ordinary. It’s average-sized, with a smooth tracking surface and predictable top-hinged mechanical clicks, though those clicks are louder than I prefer.
Audio on the Alienware 16X Aurora
The Aurora’s speakers are serviceable but unremarkable. Their placement on the sides of the palm rest creates a decent stereo effect, and output is clean enough, with no obvious tinniness and adequate volume for personal listening. In Phil Collins’ “Don’t Lose My Number,” however, drum hits lacked low-end impact, even though vocals came through clearly and instrument separation was strong.
Movies and games fare better with the Dolby app’s Movie and Gaming modes since they boost the sense of surround sound and help the sound feel fuller, but the weak bass still holds back the overall experience.
Upgradeability of the Alienware 16X Aurora
The Aurora is about as upgradeable as laptops get. Opening it up is mostly straightforward - undo the Philips-head screws in the bottom cover, then use a plastic pry tool to pop the clips around the edges. Not all the screws are the same size, and the rear corners are captive and don’t come out.
Upgrades include two DDR5 SO-DIMM slots under the square black shield between the cooling fans, two M.2 2280 drive slots, an M.2 2230 wireless card, and the 96 Whr battery.
Battery Life on the Alienware 16X Aurora
Our battery testing consists of web browsing, running OpenGL tests, and streaming videos with the screen at 150 nits while connected to Wi-Fi. The Aurora’s time of 7 hours and 58 minutes is middling, outlasting only the Asus (6:57). The Gigabyte (9:13) and the Acer (10:17) both lasted several hours longer.
Heat on the Alienware 16X Aurora
During our 15-loop Metro Exodus stress test, surface temperatures on the Aurora were 101 degrees Fahrenheit (F) between the G and H keys, 83 F on the touchpad, and 101 F on the underside around the exhaust vents.
Internally, the Core Ultra 7 270HX plus averaged 67 Celsius (C) while the RTX 5060 ran at 73 C.
Webcam on the Alienware 16X Aurora
Alienware’s 1080p webcam shows slight grain and the image looks slightly over-sharpened, but the picture is well-exposed, colorful, and doesn’t blow out highlights. It’s missing a privacy shutter, but that’s not unusual for a gaming laptop. It does, however, include an IR sensor for facial recognition logins via Windows Hello.
Software and Warranty on the Alienware 16X Aurora
The Aurora’s main app is Alienware Command Center, which brings system monitoring, power profiles, keyboard lighting, and game library management into one place. Its power presets cover battery, quiet, balanced, and performance modes, while AlienFX handles the single-zone RGB keyboard effects. The app also links out to Dolby for audio tuning. Dell SupportAssist is also included for support access and system updates.
The laptop is backed by a one-year warranty.
Alienware 16X Aurora Configurations
We tested the 16X Aurora in a mildly upgraded configuration, which pairs a Core Ultra 7 270HX processor with an RTX 5060 GPU, 16GB of RAM, and a 1TB SSD. It retails for $2,279.99 from Dell, though I saw it as low as $1,679.99 during our review period. The base model drops to a 512GB SSD and retails for $1,529.99.
Available upgrades include a Core Ultra 9 290HX CPU and RTX 5070 or RTX 5070 Ti graphics. Adding both the Ultra 9 and the 5070 Ti pushes the price to $3,029.99. The memory tops out at 64GB (two 32GB modules) and storage drives are available up to 4TB (two 2TB drives in RAID 0).
Standard features across all models include the 16-inch 2560 x 1600 OLED display, 96 Whr battery, single-zone keyboard backlighting, and Wi-Fi 7.
Dell’s pricing seems to align with the market – I found various other gaming laptops featuring a Core HX-class CPU, a premium screen, and an RTX 5060 or RTX 5070 for within about $100 of what the Aurora commanded.
Bottom Line
The Alienware 16X Aurora is a highly competent gaming laptop with a clear highlight: its superb 16-inch OLED display. It pairs solid gaming performance with reassuring build quality, practical connectivity, and strong upgradeability, while avoiding any major pitfalls. Portability is the main tradeoff, as its weight, size, and middling battery life make it feel more like a desktop replacement than an everyday carry than something like the Razer Blade 16. But if you want a sturdy, capable 16-inch gaming system with a gorgeous screen and few real compromises, the Aurora is easy to recommend.
Charles Jefferies is a freelance reviewer for Tom’s Hardware US. He covers laptop and desktop PCs, especially gaming models.

articles.title: Versteckte Kameras leichter finden
articles.text:
In Airbnb oder Hotel: Mit diesem Smartphone-Aufsatz findest du versteckte Kameras
Seit Jahren kursieren Berichte von Urlauber:innen, die in ihren Airbnb-Wohnungen oder Hotelzimmern versteckte Kameras finden. Diese sind oft in Lüftungsschächten, Klimaanlagen oder Rauchmeldern untergebracht. Mittlerweile gibt es eine Reihe von Maßnahmen, die man ergreifen kann, um solche Kameras aufzuspüren.
SweepLED soll versteckte Kameras finden
Allerdings gehört dazu etwa das aufwändige Absuchen der möglicherweise betroffenen Räume oder die Überprüfung von WLAN- und Bluetooth-Verbindungen auf verdächtige Datentransfers oder Geräte. Deutlich einfacher soll die Suche nach versteckten Kameras künftig mit dem sogenannten SweepLED funktionieren.
Das von Forscher:innen aus Südkorea und Singapur gemeinsam entwickelte System soll eine Genauigkeit von 94 Prozent erreichen. Das übertrifft schon vorhandene portable Detektoren deutlich. Auch weil diese oft Reflexionen von Metall, Glas oder Plastikoberflächen fälschlicherweise für Kameralinsen halten, wie es in einer entsprechenden Mitteilung der Forscher:innen heißt.
Hohe Trefferquote dank LEDs und KI
SweepLED erreicht die hohe Trefferquote durch eine Kombination mehrerer LEDs, die an das Smartphone angebracht, Lichtimpulse in die Umgebung abgeben. Dort werden sie reflektiert und diese Reflexionen von einer KI ausgewertet, wie die Forscher:innen in einem Paper erklären.
Dabei spielt den Forscher:innen in die Hände, dass Licht von Kameralinsen anders reflektiert wird als etwa von Glas- oder Metalloberflächen. Die KI soll diese Unterschiede in wenigen Sekunden ausmachen können. Getestet haben die Forscher:innen das neue System an 30 Gegenständen, darunter neben versteckten Kameras auch an gewöhnlich reflektierenden Objekten wie Ladegeräten, Uhren oder Fernbedienungen.
Erkennungstechnologie für Nicht-Experten
„Versteckte Kameras stellen eine ernsthafte Bedrohung für die persönliche Sicherheit und die Privatsphäre im Alltag dar“, erklärt Mitautor Jun Han von der KAIST School of Computing. Die Lösung der Forscher:innen basiere dagegen auf kostengünstiger Hardware für Smartphones und KI-Analyse. Dadurch, so Han, könne diese „praktische Erkennungstechnologie“ auch von Nicht-Expert:innen genutzt werden.
Den Forscher:inne zufolge soll die benötigte Hardware lediglich mit Kosten von rund sechs Euro zu Buche schlagen. Allerdings gibt es das SweepLED noch nicht als fertiges Produkt, sondern bisher nur als Prototyp.

articles.title: JBL Quantum : 4 nouveaux casques gaming pour submerger la concurrence
articles.text:
Chaque année, JBL met à jour sa gamme de casques gaming Quantum à l’occasion de la Gamescom. 2026 est à ce titre une cuvée assez pragmatique, où tous les utilisateurs ou presque pourraient trouver leur bonheur : le modèle haut de gamme Quantum 850, le casque milieu de gamme Quantum 520, et l’entrée de gamme filaire Quantum 120.
Produit le plus ambitieux et le plus complet du lot, le JBL Quantum 850 mise sur une conception confortable, une quadruple connectivité, et sur un ambitieux suivi des mouvements de la tête. Plus abordables, le Quantum 520 et sa variante 520X (version Xbox) s’appuient sur une architecture sonore poussée, une triple connectivité, et sur une prise en charge du Spatial Sound. Enfin, le Quantum 120 se présente comme une introduction filaire à l’univers gaming Quantum, introduction qui n’a pourtant rien de gadget.
JBl Quantum 850 : le haut de gamme à peine simplifié
Rien de révolutionnaire, le Quantum 850 affiche le design très gaming (pas du tout nomade) des précédents casques haut de gamme Quantum, 950 en tête, avec notamment de larges coussinets circum auriculaires, des jeux de leds, un micro flexible détachable, et un repose-tête flottant façon hamac. Moins poussé qu’un Quantum 950, il dispose toutefois d’une batterie remplaçable (mais pas d’une base multifonction avec recharge), et de transducteurs dynamiques de 50 mm avec revêtement carbone. Notons qu’outre la batterie, de nombreuses pièces (hamac, coussinets, microphones, coques) sont remplaçables.
Sorte de produit ultra-polyvalent, le casque peut se connecter de quatre manières : dongle USB-C pour du sans-fil basse-latence, Bluetooth 5.3, filaire en USB-C, et filaire en jack 3,5 mm. Cerise sur le gâteau pour les télétravailleurs, la certification Zoom.
Difficile de faire plus complet, d’autant que le JBL Quantum 850 dispose même d’un système de réduction de bruit active, et d’une fonction 3D avec suivi des mouvements de la tête. Comme souvent, seuls les joueurs Xbox sont laissés sur la touche, le dongle n’étant pas compatible avec l’écosystème
Disponible d’ici quelques jours, le JBL Quantum 850 sera vendu à 279,99 euros.
JBL Quantum 520 et Quantum 520X : presque tout, à moins de 100 euros
Plus simples mais ne manquant pas de style, les Quantum 520 et Quantum 520X sont eux-aussi des casques de gaming sans-fil très polyvalents, puisqu’équipés d’un dongle USB-C, d’une puce Bluetooth 5.4, et d’une interface audio sur le port USB-C. La marque surprend légèrement, en intégrant des pièces transparentes à l’extérieur des coques, d’où cette apparence très légère.
Si JBL met en avant ses transducteurs de 50 mm revêtus de carbone, à priori proches de ceux équipant le Quantum 850, de nombreuses fonctions disparaissent fort logiquement : mode 3D mais suivi des mouvements de la tête, pas de repose-tête flottant, pas de batterie remplaçable, pas de coques ni de coussinets remplaçables, pas de réduction de bruit active. Bien sûr, les deux appareils sont compatibles avec l’application QuantumEngine, qui offrira un haut degré de personnalisation.
Identique techniquement au Quantum 520, le Quantum 520X apporte tout simplement la compatibilité avec l’environnement Xbox. Les deux casques sont déjà disponibles, pour 99,99 euros.
Quantum 120 : pour une expérience quantique à prix plancher
Dernier-né de la fratrie et sorte de petit frère filaire et passif des 520, le JBL Quantum 120 est une création d’entrée de gamme qui ne manque pas d’arguments. Très simple sur la forme, bien que conservant une approche circum-auriculaire, ce casque très léger peut compter sur la présence de transducteurs de 50 mm avec membrane carbone, et sur un microphone détachable avec cellule de 6 mm. Sa connectivité se limite à la très universelle (avec des guillemets) prise jack 3,5 mm, mais le casque peut malgré tout profiter des avantages de l’application QuantumEngine (la marque ne précise pas de quelle manière).
Déjà disponible dès maintenant, le JBL Quantum 120 est vendu à 44,99 euros.

articles.title: Filigran adds attack chaining to OpenAEV for automated penetration testing - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Filigran adds attack chaining to OpenAEV for automated penetration testing
French cybersecurity company Filigran SAS today launched Attack Chaining, a capability in its OpenAEV exposure validation product that links individual attack simulations into a single running path. It ships with OpenAEV v3, out today.
Real intrusions rarely stop at one technique. Reconnaissance finds a target, a credential dump hands over a password and that password opens the next machine, with every step depending on whatever the last one turned up. Single-technique tests and prewritten scenarios catch specific weaknesses well enough. Neither adjusts to what an attacker finds partway through.
Each action feeds the next one. OpenAEV logs what an action turns up as a structured record, whether that is a password, an open port or a set of permissions, and the engine reads it at runtime to work out the next move. A working credential pushes the run deeper into the network. The runs branch where more than one route forward exists, and any control that blocks a step ends the chain there. Teams can assemble that logic themselves out of techniques, payloads or custom actions, then set conditions on each hop.
The run appears on an interactive graph while it happens, tracking pivots and branches from the first action through to the objective. Drilling into a finding shows why an action fired. Filigran said the graph is meant to expose chokepoints, the single step whose removal collapses an entire path, so a team can fix one control instead of triaging the whole chain.
Two modes sit on the same engine. An operator can build the logic and step through execution manually. In agent-led mode the objective and scope are set in plain language, and an artificial intelligence agent builds and adapts the chain itself, generating phishing emails and landing pages for social engineering steps.
“Security validation has to evolve with the way attackers operate,” said co-founder Julien Richard. “The goal is no longer just to prove that we can block individual techniques; it is to understand whether those techniques can be combined into a path that leads to a real compromise.”
Jean-Philippe Salles, vice president of product management at the company, said a validation outcome is “only actionable when security teams can trace the logic that generated it.”
Filigran’s “State of Threat Management” survey of 550 security decision-makers and practitioners found 88% relying on manual processes for offensive attack simulation. The company said 97% also have difficulty working out whether their exposures can be exploited at all.
Four other additions come with v3. A redesigned home dashboard called the Adversarial Exposure Command Center pulls posture, simulation results and detection coverage into a single view. An Adversarial Exposure Score aggregates validation results across exposure sources.
New red-teaming injectors run adversary simulations against chatbots and agents built on large language models, using the same engine that validates endpoint and email defenses. Reporting is now one click to a PDF.
OpenAEV v3 is available to all users today. Attack Chaining is limited to the Enterprise Edition.
Founded in 2022, Filigran has raised more than $100 million in funding, including rounds of $35 million in October 2024 and $58 million in October 2025. Investors in the company include Eurazeo SE, Insight Partners LP, Accel Partners LP and Deutsche Telekom AG.

articles.title: Samsung Expands the Galaxy Book6 Lineup With a More Accessible Model
articles.text:
Tuesday, September 1st 2026
	
									
	
	
	
Samsung Expands the Galaxy Book6 Lineup With a More Accessible Model
Samsung Electronics today announced a new 14-inch Galaxy Book6, expanding the Galaxy Book6 lineup with a more accessible model designed for everyday computing. Starting at $799, Galaxy Book6 combines up to 25 hours of battery life, Intel Core 3 and Core 5 performance, Galaxy AI-enabled features, and the design language of the Galaxy Book6 family.
"With the new Galaxy Book6, we wanted to make the Galaxy Book experience available for more people," said Mincheol Lee, EVP, Head of Galaxy Ecosystems Business Team at Samsung Electronics. "At a more accessible price, it brings together the everyday essentials users value, including dependable performance, long-lasting battery life, connected Galaxy experiences, and Galaxy Book6's design DNA, giving users confidence that lasts beyond the purchase."Performance and Battery for Everyday Use
The new Galaxy Book6 is designed around the tasks people rely on every day, from browsing the web and creating documents to video calls, multitasking, and streaming content. With up to 25 hours of battery life on a single charge, users can work, study, and enjoy content for longer throughout the day. When it is time to power up, 45 W fast charging provides approximately 33% charge in 30 minutes.
That long-lasting power is paired with Intel Core Series 3 processor performance, bringing Intel's latest architecture and power efficiency to essential PC experiences. The processor also supports Galaxy AI and other AI features designed to help users work, create, and get things done more easily.Built With Galaxy Book6 Design DNA
The latest addition to the Galaxy Book6 lineup carries forward the design language of the series, defined by clean, balanced lines and a symmetrical design. A centered logo further reinforces a unified Galaxy Book6 identity.
At 15.7 mm thin and 1.35 kg, Galaxy Book6 combines a slim profile with portability that makes it easy to carry throughout the day, from home and school to work and travel. For the first time on Galaxy Book, Violet Silver brings a fresh expression to the lineup, adding a distinctive touch to the clean, understated Galaxy Book6 design. A classic Gray option is also available.
The 16:10 display provides more vertical viewing space for documents, web pages, and multitasking, while anti-reflective technology minimizes glare for clearer, more comfortable viewing wherever you are. Galaxy Book6 also keeps commonly used connections close at hand.Its two USB Type-C ports offer the same functionality, so users can connect with less guesswork, while USB Type-A, HDMI 1.4, and a 3.5 mm headphone jack, give users a versatile range of connectivity for displays, peripherals, and accessories without relying on additional dongles.
Galaxy Experiences That Work Better Together
The Galaxy Book6 brings together Galaxy AI and connected experiences across Galaxy devices to make it easier to find information, move content and work across screens.
AI Select lets users select content directly on the screen and instantly access helpful information and insights while browsing, shopping, or viewing content online. It also includes AI cut out, which lets users instantly remove image backgrounds to prepare polished visuals for presentations, e-commerce listings, or marketing materials. Note Assist summarizes notes and surfaces key information so users can review important details faster.
Content also moves more easily across Galaxy devices. Quick Share enables fast file sharing between compatible devices, while Storage Share lets users access photos, videos, and files across compatible Galaxy smartphones and Galaxy Book without transferring them first—making it easier to bring content from a phone directly into a document, presentation, or creative project.Galaxy Book6 also helps users work naturally across screens. Multi Control allows a single keyboard and mouse to control multiple supported Galaxy devices, while Second Screen turns a Galaxy Tab into an additional display. Nearby Devices simplifies device discovery and connection, and Link to Windows extends supported Galaxy smartphone experiences to the PC.
Together, Galaxy AI and connected Galaxy experiences reduce the steps between devices, helping users stay focused as information, content, and work move more seamlessly across the Galaxy ecosystem.
Confidence That Lasts Beyond the Purchase
Galaxy Book6 is backed by Samsung's commitment to long-term reliability, with quality, durability, and support designed to give users confidence over time. Every Galaxy Book6 undergoes rigorous durability and quality testing to meet Samsung's highest standards. For added peace of mind, Samsung Care+ offers comprehensive coverage for accidental damage, repairs, and replacements, helping users feel more confident throughout the life of their PC.
Availability
Galaxy Book6 is available in select markets, with additional markets to follow. Starting at $799, it offers 8 GB or 16 GB of memory and 256 GB, 512 GB, or 1 TB SSD storage options. Availability, specifications, colors, features, and supported experiences may vary by region.

articles.title: The Cosori Dual Blaze Twinfry Compact is much more than just an air fryer — it's packed with cooking features, and very reasonably priced.
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
This big basket air fryer comes with a useful cookbook in the box, additional cooking modes such as roast and grill, and intuitive controls for easy operation, all at a reasonable price. It's not the biggest basket on the market, nor does it deliver the very best results, but as an all-round package it's an air fryer I'd happily recommend.
Pros
- +Excellent results from versatile cooking modes
- +Useful quick start guide and cook book included in box
- +Intuitive controls and dishwasher-safe basket
Cons
- -Large footprint not so good for small kitchens
- -Takes time to understand cooking times
- -No shake reminder or basket window
Why you can trust TechRadar
Cosori Dual Blaze Twinfry Compact: 30-second review
The Cosori Dual Blaze Twinfry Compact might be a bit of a mouthful to say, but there's plenty to like about this air fryer.
Things start off well when you open the box with a useful quick start guide and fun little cookbook with over 20 recipes, showing you the range of possibilities available with this appliance.
With roast, grill and bake modes alongside the standard air fry function, and with an 8.6L basket that also has a divider so you can cook two things simultaneously, the Twinfry Compact could replace multiple appliances in your kitchen.
From crispy chicken wings, roast potatoes and wonderfully baked cakes, to gooey cookies, grilled burgers, and reheated pizza, I enjoyed using this air fryer.
The controls are straight forward, the basket is easy to clean, and it's not going to set you back as much as some of the more premium machines - while giving you results which are almost as good as expensive rivals.
It's a large device, so those with smaller kitchens might struggle to fit it in, while the lack of a shake reminder means you'll need to be vigilant when it's in use to make sure your food is turned/tossed correctly.
But these are minor points against what is a very capable air fryer, and one you should consider buying — especially if you can find it discounted.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Cosori Dual Blaze Twinfry Compact: price and availability
- £159.99, but I’ve seen it discounted to £130
- This model isn't available in the US and Australia
The Cosori Dual Blaze Twinfry Compact Air Fryer price is £159.99, putting it in the middle of the larger-basket market, although I have seen it discounted to £130 at some retailers, so it’s worth shopping around to find the best price.
That means the Twinfry Compact finds itself up against some strong competition, including the Philips 1000 Series Dual Basket and Tower Elite 11 Litre Flexi Drawer.
The list price equates to around $220 / AU$300, but this particular model isn't available in the US and Australia.
- Value score: 4.5/5
Cosori Dual Blaze Twinfry Compact: specifications
| Review Model | CAF-TF801-AUK | 
| Number of baskets | 1 | 
| Number of cooking programs | 6 | 
| Cooking programs | Air Fry, Roast, Grill, Bake, Reheat, Dry | 
| Extra functions | Dual Zone with Removable Divider, DualBlaze Tech | 
| Smart control | No | 
| Wattage | 2700W | 
| Capacity | 8.6L | 
| Temperature range | 35-240C | 
| Time range | 1 minute - 4 hours | 
| Dimensions | 339cm (D) x 482cm (W) x 281cm (H) | 
| Dishwasher-safe | Yes | 
| Weight | 8kg | 
Cosori Dual Blaze Twinfry Compact: design
- Well designed with clear buttons and useful quick-start guide
- You can split the basket in two, and there are six preset modes
- No shake reminder or window on the basket
The Cosori Dual Blaze Twinfry Compact Air Fryer is nicely designed, with a sleek matte finish and clear controls. Sure it’s on the larger side, but the sizable 8.6L basket has to go somewhere.
It does mean you’ll need a chunk of worksurface space to fit the 339cm (D) x 482cm (W) x 281cm (H) machine, so those with smaller kitchens might find it a struggle to comfortably place this air fryer, or have enough space in a cupboard to store it. If you are tight on counter space, consider a smaller basket air fryer, or a vertically stacked, dual-basket option such as the Philips 4000 Series Stacked Dual Basket or Ninja Double Stack XL.
You can split the 8.6L basket into two 4.3L offerings with the included divider in the box. This allows you to cook two separate foods, at different settings, simultaneously, offering greater flexibility.
Get past the size though, and there’s a lot to like. I was particularly impressed with the quick start guide in the box, which explained the main functions clearly and offered up a big table of different foods with the best cooking mode, temperature and time. This makes it really easy to get cooking.
What helps the Cosori Dual Blaze Twinfry Compact stand out from the crowd however, is its four heating elements. Two above, and two below the basket, providing even heat above and below your food, for an improved cook.
You get six preset cooking modes too, with Air Fry, Roast, Grill, Bake, Reheat, and Dry - but there are no food-specific presets like you see on some air fryers.
I do like the button layout on this appliance, with clearly labelled buttons making it easy to select if you’re cooking on one side of the basket, or doing a large batch in the whole thing — Cosori calls this the 'grandzone'.
Temperature and time are easily adjusted with up and down arrow buttons, while the ‘match’ button can copy the settings from one side of the basket to the other, and sync allows you to cook two foods in each side of the basket for different durations, but have them finish at the same time by delaying the start of the side with the shorter time.
There’s no shake reminder though, which is a small miss as you need to remember to shake or turn the food yourself. There’s also no window on the basket, so you can’t keep an eye on the food while it cooks, you have to remove the basket which pauses cooking.
When you come to remove the basket from the air fryer, the large handle that runs the full width of the basket makes it easy to grip and move around. Although, if you’ve loaded up the basket with food it can be heavy, so you’ll need to use both hands.
Before you put any food in the air fryer for the first time though, you need to wash the basket and pop the air fryer through a test run. The manual says to run the Cosori Dual Blaze Twinfry Compact for five minutes at 200C (give the basket, divider and trays a quick wash first) to ensure it's working and to remove any residue on components. During this time it will smell a bit, but don’t worry as it’s doing what it needs to.
Cleaning is pretty easy too. The basket, divider and trays are all dishwasher safe, while you can also hand wash them with warm water, mild soap, and a non-abrasive sponge. The size of the basket does mean washing it in smaller kitchen sinks can be a touch tricky, but it’s not a huge issue.
- Design score: 4.5/5
Cosori Dual Blaze Twinfry Compact: performance
- Great results from air fry, bake, grill and roast modes
- It takes time to fully understand the best temps and timings
- Opt for shorter cook times, to avoid burning food
At 60dB (from my own tests), the fans on this air fryer are noisier than some, so you’ll be well aware that it’s on and cooking. It’s not loud enough to drown out conversation, but you might want to take a step or two away from it if you are chatting to someone.
Whenever I review a large basket air fryer one of my go-to first cooks is pizza. When I tested the Tower Elite 11 Litre Flexi Drawer I was able to fit a small circular pizza in the drawer. With the Cosori, the basket isn’t as big, nor as deep as the Tower, which means I had to slice my pizza in half to fit it in the basket.
Round pizza
Cooked using Cosori Dual Blaze Twinfry Compact Air Fryer
This wasn’t an issue as it was a fresh pie, but had I purchased a frozen pizza I wouldn’t have been able to cook it in this air fryer. I selected air fry mode, set the temperature to 180C and the time to eight minutes.
After six minutes the pizza was done, with a crispy base and melted cheese making for a satisfying lunch. I returned a few days later with an oval pizza that I could easily fit in the basket. Another six minutes at 180C and again I had a nicely cooked pizza. It’s quicker and easier than using the oven.
Frozen fries
Cooked using Cosori Dual Blaze Twinfry Compact Air Fryer
I was also able to air fry a large batch of delicious homemade fries (200C for 20 minutes), that came out wonderfully crispy on the outside while remaining fluffy in the middle.
Frozen fries come out equally as well, with the same temperature and duration as their homemade counterparts to achieve a similar cook. The adjustment I made when I came to cook fries again was to reduce the time by a couple of minutes, to avoid the outside of the fries being quite so well done.
Chicken wings
Cooked using Cosori Dual Blaze Twinfry Compact Air Fryer
Chicken wings, coated in a buffalo ranch rub, came out with wonderfully crispy skin and succulent meat after 20 minutes at 185C.
I was able to fit eight full size wings in the basket, and I might have been able to squeeze one or two more in if I bunch them up a bit, but I didn't want to compromise the cook.
While they were very good, they weren't quite as moist inside as the wings I steam fried in the Philips 5000 series.
Cookie cup
Baked using Cosori Dual Blaze Twinfry Compact Air Fryer
I also tried a Marks & Spencer cookie cup, currently doing the rounds on social in the UK as a must-try air fryer treat. I went for the Smores Cookie cup, and after 10 minutes in zone 1 (the left side of the basket) at 160C I got a cup that oozed chocolate topped with nicely toasted marshmallows.
And while we’re on the subject of sweet treats, the bake mode was another favorite of mine, with the Cosori Dual Blaze Twinfry Compact capable of excellent results. I cooked a simple banana bread in the grandzone for 25 minutes at 160C, and a further 20 minutes at 140C.
It rose wonderfully, and delivered an excellent bake that was soft, fluffy and flavourful. I also whipped up a batch of cookies, and on the bake mode for eight minutes at 175C I was treated to gooey-centered delights with a crispy exterior. The cook on them wasn't quite as impressive as the more premium Philips 5000 series I had recently tested, but they were still tasty.
Banana bread
Baked using Cosori Dual Blaze Twinfry Compact Air Fryer
The roast mode is also a useful addition. I was able to cook fluffy roast potatoes (with a reasonably crispy exterior) in less time, and using less power than my oven. And there was no need to par boil them either.
I cooked them for 25 minutes at 200C using the roast mode, and while you'll get crispier results using an oven, the Cosori is a great option when you're looking for faster results.
I roasted the potatoes alongside broccoli and sprouts, using the divider so the vegetables could be cooked for 15 minutes at 190C (per Cosori’s own instructions).
This turned out to be too long, as after 10 minutes they were already overcooked. An example of the initial trial and error required when understanding a new air fryer. However, for chunkier veg — such as carrots and parsnips - this setting works much better.
One of the slightly more unusual cooking modes available here is grill, but it works surprisingly well. I tested it out with four beef burgers, with the quick start guide that came with the air fryer suggesting I cook them for 11 minutes at 230C.
I was initially worried when I pulled them out at the end that they could be overcooked, but I was happy to find they were still juicy in the middle. You wouldn’t know it was the work of an air fryer rather than a traditional grill, and it was incredibly easy to do.
If you are someone who grills a lot, the Cosori Dual Blaze Twinfry Compact can replace your traditional grill, as well as being a strong air fryer and baking machine.
Burgers
Cooked using Cosori Dual Blaze Twinfry Compact Air Fryer
Something I did notice was you want to lean towards the shorter end of cooking times, because if forget about the air fryer, or set the timer for the higher end of a cooking range, you might find food gets a little cremated.
This is all part of the air fryer ownership journey, and during the first couple of weeks you’ll need to spend some time closely monitoring how quickly food is cooking to get a better understanding of the performance.
The lack of a shake reminder means it’s easier to forget about checking how your food is getting. But don’t let this put you off. All air fryers come with this learning curve, and with the Cosori Dual Blaze Twinfry Compact less tends to be more when it comes to cooking duration.
- Performance score: 4.5/5
Should you buy the Cosori Dual Blaze Twinfry Compact?
| Report card |  |  | 
|---|---|---|
| Attribute | Notes | Rating | 
| Value | There’s great versatility here, with the bake and grill modes excellent additions alongside air fry. And with deals to be had, you can probably get it for less than RRP is you shop around. | 4.5/5 | 
| Design | A slick design that looks smart on the kitchen counter, so long as you have space for this wide machine. Buttons are well laid out, the basket divider allows two different foods to be cooked together, and the quick start guide is packed with useful info. | 4.5/5 | 
| Performance | The Cosori Dual Blaze Twinfry Compact delivers consistent results across air fry, bake, grill and roast modes. You will need to keep an eye on things and adjust timings to suit your needs, but once you’ve mastered this you’ll be happy with the results. | 4.5/5 | 
Buy it if
You love big basket flexibility
The big basket on the Cosori Dual Blaze Twinfry Compact can fit plenty of food in it. Whether it’s a large joint of meat, or a smaller main and a side split by the divider and cooked at different temps, you can do it with this air fryer.
You want more than just an air fryer
With impressive bake, roast and grill modes, the Cosori Dual Blaze Twinfry Compact can handle more than just simple air frying. You could reduce the number of appliances in your kitchen.
You don’t want to spend loads
WIth an already reasonable price tag, and with discounts to be had if you shop around, the Cosori Dual Blaze Twinfry Compact delivers great versatility and features for the price. You can spend more on premium rivals from Philips and Ninja, but aside from sleeker designs and food presets, the difference it’s overly great.
Don’t buy it if
You’re forgetful
There’s no shake reminder here, nor is there a window in the basket, which means you really need to remember to check how your food is cooking. Otherwise you might end up with over cooked items, or uneven cooking if you forget to flip, turn, or shake the food in the basket.
You have limited counter space
Due to the sizable basket of this air fryer, you’re looking at a wide footprint. For kitchens that have limited space on counters, this Cosori might be too big for your setup. Consider a smaller basket air fryer, or a stacked offering that reduces the footprint required.
You want a quiet air fryer
The Cosori Dual Blaze Twinfry Compact isn’t obnoxiously loud, but it is noisier than some other air fryers. If you want a quieter machine, you’ll be best off looking elsewhere.
Cosori Dual Blaze Twinfry Compact: also consider
Tower Elite 11 Litre Flexi Drawer
This air fryer has an even bigger basket, and a lower price tag, making it an excellent choice for families on a budget. Its controls aren’t as intuitive, and the basket is handwash only, but results are still good.
For more information, check out our full Tower Elite 11 Litre Flexi Drawer review
Philips 5000 Series Megabasket with Steam Air Fryer
If your budget can stretch to a premium model, this Philips large-basket air fryer also offers a great array of cooking modes, including an impressive steam function that’s made some of the best chicken wings I’ve ever had.
For more information, check out our full Philips 5000 Series Megabasket with Steam review
How I tested the Cosori Dual Blaze Twinfry Compact
- I used the Cosori Dual Blaze Twinfry Compact for multiple weeks in my kitchen
- I cooked a variety of food, including fries, cakes, vegetables, pizza and meat
- I tested the various cooking modes, and the cleaning process
For my review of the Cosori Dual Blaze Twinfry Compact Air Fryer, I used it for a number of weeks at home, cooking a wide variety of food and testing out the various functions.
I baked cakes and cookies, air fried fries, chicken wings and pizza, roasted potatoes and vegetables, and grilled kebabs and burgers. I even reheated leftover pizza the next day - which was sensational on a slight hangover.
I also hand-washed the components, and ran them through a dishwasher, to ensure cleaning and maintenance was easy.
First reviewed September 2026

articles.title: Nvidia's controversial DLSS 5 will launch September 3 with NBA2K27, company shares first benchmarks — available on all RTX 50 series GPUs, laptops, and GeForce NOW
articles.text:
Nvidia's controversial DLSS 5 will launch September 3 with NBA2K27, company shares first benchmarks — available on all RTX 50 series GPUs, laptops, and GeForce NOW
The DLL leaked inside this title just days ago
Following its announcement earlier this year, and just days after the DLL leaked inside NBA2K27, Nvidia has today confirmed that its controversial DLSS 5 will launch on September 3. Starting at 9 pm PT, the aforementioned NBA title will support DLSS 5 for all RTX 50 Series GPUs, laptops, and GeForce NOW. The company also shared its first in-house benchmarks of DLSS 5, which is expected to impact GPU performance.
As a series not primarily renowned for its graphical fidelity, NBA2K27 marks a fairly strange launch title for the tech, but Nvidia says that it has closely partnered with Visual Concepts and 2K to achieve "a new level of authentic sports experience for its players." The technology, which Nvidia officially dubs as 3D-guided Neural Rendering," will reportedly show players the natural passing of light through players' ears, light catching hair, and the natural lighting of skin "all while preserving the facial geometry scanned from real-world athletes."
DLSS 5 is not without controversy. As we explained during our first look at DLSS 5 back in March, DLSS 5's AI model "is trained to infer how certain complex features of game scenes like characters, skin, hair, and environmental lighting “should” look in the real world given certain inputs from the game engine (including, but not limited to, the color buffer and motion vectors) in combination with an input frame." While deep integration with a game's engine and assets should make it more consistent and predictable than run-of-the-mill generative AI imagery, that promise hasn't stopped some critics from raising severe objections to its premise since its initial reveal.
CEO Jensen Huang described DLSS 5 as "the GPT moment for graphics — blending hand-crafted rendering with generative AI to deliver a dramatic leap in visual realism while preserving the control artists need for creative expression.”
Its launch in NBA2K27 will mark the first time the technology debuts in a playable title, marking our first "fair" assessment of its capabilities.
DLSS 5 is very resource-intensive, with early testing and indications hinting at quite severe drops in frame rate when using the tech. As expected, Nvidia has confirmed DLSS 5 will only work with RTX 50-series GPUs and mobile GPUs, as well as through GeForce Now. Other older generation cards are left out in the cold for now. Along with the announcement, Nvidia has shared its first in-house benchmarks of DLSS 5 RTX Desktop performance.
While these are difficult to contextualize (they only show one game) and should be taken with the usual grain of salt for marketing material, they are interesting in one clear sense. Nvidia has pointedly only shared 4K results for its RTX 5090 and 5080, possibly hinting at the company's expectations of diminished results on anything less powerful, though cards lower in the stack do appear below 4K resolutions.

articles.title: Google's Android update tackles motion sickness, accessibility, and more | TechCrunch
articles.text:
On Tuesday, Google announced it’s rolling out five new updates designed to make Android phones more accessible, useful, and personalized. Announced in a blog post, the features include those aimed at reducing motion sickness, helping blind and low-vision users navigate their surroundings, remembering where users leave important items, and another that adds new ways to personalize Google Messages.
While some of the features see Google playing catch-up to Apple, which already offers similar features for iPhone users, others specifically leverage Gemini to provide various improvements.
The most interesting update is “Motion Assist,” a feature designed to help people who experience motion sickness while using their phones in a moving vehicle. It adds a bubble overlay to the screen that moves in response to the vehicle’s motion, helping reduce the disconnect between what users see on their screens and what their bodies feel.
The concept isn’t entirely new, however. Apple introduced “Vehicle Motion Cues” in 2024, which uses animated dots around the edges of the display that move in response to a vehicle’s motion.
Users can set “Motion Assist” to turn on automatically, add it to Quick Settings, and customize the bubble’s shape, color, and transparency. Google says this feature is available to Android 17 users.
Google is also introducing “Guided Vision,” a feature designed with blind and low-vision users in mind. It combines the phone’s camera with Gemini to help with tasks such as reading small print on a food label, viewing a menu in a dark restaurant, or identifying objects around the house.
The feature can also provide voice guidance when the camera isn’t positioned correctly, telling users to move the phone, pan around, or center an object. Guided Vision is coming to phones running Android 9 and newer in countries where Gemini is available.
Another update gives Gemini a new way to help users remember where they put important items. A “remembered items” section in Find Hub will allow users to tell Gemini where they’ve stored something. For example, a user could say they put their passport in a bedroom drawer, and Gemini can save that information in Find Hub. Users can also attach a photo to make the item easier to identify later.
Additionally, Google is adding a Google Keep integration to Google Messages, allowing people to share and edit grocery lists, vacation notes, and other information directly within a conversation.
Plus, Google Messages is getting more personalization options. Users will be able to customize individual chats with backgrounds, photos, and colors, Google says. The text bubbles will automatically match.
Apple added a similar custom background feature to Messages last year.

articles.title: En Zaragoza, una inquilina dejó de pagar el alquiler, se hizo okupa y consiguió que la propietaria le pagara 1.000 euros de agua
articles.text:
María Marcuello llevaba 15 años viviendo en un piso de la calle Eugenio Lucas, en Zaragoza. Se mudó a Barcelona por motivos personales y decidió alquilarlo por unos 600 euros al mes. Todo fue bien hasta noviembre de 2024: la inquilina, identificada como M.C.S.R., dejó de pagar y se convirtió en okupa de la noche a la mañana. El Juzgado de Primera Instancia n.º 17 de Zaragoza ha ordenado ahora el lanzamiento judicial del inmueble para el próximo 9 de octubre, tras casi dos años de pleitos y un agujero enorme en facturas no abonadas.
La pesadilla logística. Varios medios apuntan a que la inquilina llegó a tener ingresos superiores a los de la propietaria, pero decidió no destinarlos al alquiler. Hasta que dejó los grifos abiertos: la factura de agua ascendió a casi 1.000 euros y se cargó directamente contra la propietaria, que sigue siendo titular del suministro. Sumado al alquiler impagado, la deuda total ronda ya los 15.000 euros. Al parecer, María no ha visto ni un céntimo desde hace casi dos años.
Lo que dice la ley. La okupación no es un delito. Lo que sí es, según el Código Penal, es la usurpación de bien inmueble, artículo 245.2, penado con multa de tres a seis meses por tratarse de un delito leve. Desde el 2 de enero de 2025, la Ley Orgánica 1/2025 reformó la Lecrim para derivar estos casos —junto al allanamiento de morada, es decir, invadir sin consentimiento el lugar primario donde moras— hacia diligencias urgentes, en vez del procedimiento de delitos leves.
El objetivo de estos cambios era acelerar el desalojo en primeras viviendas. Este caso concreto ha tardado más de un año en resolverse porque, para los propietarios, la vía civil, con su trámite previo de conciliación obligatoria, sigue siendo más habitual que la penal.
El vacío legal. El Tribunal Supremo dictó el 24 de junio de 2026 una sentencia que fija doctrina: cortar la luz o el agua a un okupa no es delito de coacciones, siempre que quien ocupa carezca de cualquier título jurídico. La inquilina de Zaragoza sí tuvo, en su momento, contrato legítimo, así que jurídicamente sigue teniendo "un título aparente o en disputa" sobre la vivienda. Ricardo Bravo, portavoz de la Plataforma de Afectados por la Ocupación, lo resume así: "Hubo un título posesorio en un momento dado, aunque haya acabado su vigencia". Traducido: puedes cortarle el agua a un okupa pero no a un inquiokupa.
Agua usada como arma. Bravo recuerda el caso de una vecina de 97 años de Colmenar Viejo que en 2022 tuvo que pagar 2.000 euros de agua porque sus inquiokupas decidieron llenar la piscina. "Es una práctica que además se utiliza para hacer daño al propietario", explica. Sin embargo, las denuncias por allanamiento y usurpación de vivienda cayeron un 9,4% en 2025, hasta 14.875 casos, según el Ministerio del Interior. Cataluña concentra el 40% de todos los casos del país (5.913 denuncias), muy por delante de Madrid, que apenas suma el 9%. Traducido a calendario: una media de más de 40 okupaciones denunciadas cada día en toda España.
La cifra clave. Sobre 27,5 millones de viviendas en España, la okupación afecta a menos del 0,06% del parque total, según los propios datos oficiales. Estamos en máximos de uso residencial desde el boom crítico de 2008. El fenómeno es mediáticamente enorme y estadísticamente residual, dos cosas que pueden ser ciertas a la vez sin contradecirse: anecdótico en volumen, devastador para quien lo sufre en primera persona, como María.
Otro caso igual. En Torrelodones, la hijastra del actor Fernando Rey y exmujer de un futbolista del Real Madrid debe 32.000 euros a sus propietarios tras tres años sin pagar el alquiler de una casa con piscina, garaje y trastero. Otro matrimonio denunció en octubre de 2025 a la que ellos mismos apodaron "la inquilina perfecta": tres años sin pagar y 33.000 euros de deuda acumulada. Y en Carabanchel, una inquiokupa fue más lejos todavía: realquiló habitaciones de la vivienda ajena que ocupaba sin pagar, montando fiestas en el patio comunitario mientras la deuda con la propietaria real superaba los 8.000 euros.
Si bien estas cifras ni son oficiales ni se han ratificado, se estima que el Ministerio de Hacienda tenga al menos 33 inmuebles propios okupados repartidos por España, sin que la propia Administración los recupere con más agilidad que un particular. La OCU lanzó en junio de 2026 la campaña "Vivienda sin preokupación", denunciando que la prórroga de la suspensión de desahucios aprobada en pandemia se mantuvo vigente hasta bien entrado 2026, dejando a miles de propietarios con plazos judiciales que consideran inasumibles.
El término que falta. Estos son perfectos ejemplos de "inquiokupación". Nada de entrar forzando una vivienda vacía, sino a través de inquilino legítimo que deja de pagar y se resiste a marcharse, aprovechando que el desahucio por vía civil exige trámites y tiempo de prórroga. El Ministerio del Interior ni siquiera contempla esta categoría como variable propia, así que estos casos quedan mezclados en las cifras generales de impagos. El 9 de octubre, si nada se tuerce, María recuperará su piso. Los 15.000 euros de deuda, esos sí, se han ido por el sumidero.

articles.title: Test Samsung 85R95H : un TV Mini Led RGB qui délivre une claque colorimétrique, mais qui aura du mal à faire de l'ombre à l'Oled
articles.text:
| Qualité d'image |  | 
| Diagonale d'écran | 85 pouces (214 cm) | 
| Définition | 3840 x 2160 (4K) | 
| Technologie de rétroéclairage | Mini LED | 
| Formats HDR supportés | HDR10, HDR10+, HLG | 
| Jeux vidéo |  | 
| Fréquence de la dalle | 165 Hz | 
| Ergonomie |  | 
| Dimensions (L x H x P) | 1880 x 1148 x 393 mm | 
| Poids | 40 kg | 
| Connectique | 4 x HDMI, 2 x USB, Vidéocomposite, Ethernet, S/PDIF optique, Port SD | 
| Ports HDMI 2.1 | 4 | 
| Système d'exploitation | Tizen | 
| Connexion sans-fil | Bluetooth, Wi-Fi | 
| Protocoles sans-fil | AirPlay 2, Chromecast | 
| Assistant vocal intégré | Alexa, Bixby | 
| Réparabilité |  | 
| Indice de réparabilité | 8.6 /10 | 
Avec son R95H, Samsung inaugure la technologie Micro RGB sur une diagonale grand public. Couleurs étendues, pic lumineux élevé et dalle 165 Hz sont au programme, mais ce Mini-Led très haut de gamme doit faire face à des Oled ultra-efficaces.
Le Samsung 85R95H est tout simplement la version 85 pouces du 75R95H que nous avons testé il y a peu en 75 pouces. Hormis la taille, leurs caractéristiques sont identiques. Nous vous avons préparé un résumé du test ci-dessous, mais vous pouvez bien sûr lire le test complet pour en savoir plus.
Le Samsung R95H se distingue par une qualité d’image globalement très convaincante grâce à sa dalle Mini Led RGB, qui offre une excellente fidélité des couleurs dès la sortie du carton. En SDR, le mode Filmmaker affiche un Delta E moyen de 2,5, une température de couleur quasiment parfaite (6494 K) et une luminosité de 619 cd/m², assurant une image fidèle et parfaitement lisible même en plein jour. En HDR, le téléviseur conserve une très bonne précision avec un Delta E de 2,3 et atteint un pic lumineux de 2760 cd/m² sur une fenêtre de 10 %, tout en couvrant 100 % du DCI-P3 et 95,3 % du Rec.2020, un niveau exceptionnel pour un téléviseur grand public. Son filtre antireflet est également très efficace, mais ces excellentes performances sont ternies par un blooming particulièrement marqué, un banding parfois très visible et des angles de vision limités, des défauts difficiles à accepter à ce niveau de gamme.
Le R95H propose une fiche technique très solide pour le jeu vidéo avec une dalle 165 Hz, quatre ports HDMI 2.1 compatibles 4K 120 Hz, le VRR, l’ALLM et le Freesync Premium Pro. Son input lag très faible (10,7 ms à 60 Hz et 7,3 ms à 120 Hz) garantit une excellente réactivité, tandis que le mode Jeu conserve une bonne fidélité des couleurs avec un Delta E de 3,2 en SDR et 2,1 en HDR. En revanche, la rémanence reste supérieure à celle d’un téléviseur Oled, ce qui se traduit par davantage de traînées dans les mouvements rapides.
La partie audio délivre un résultat satisfaisant avec des basses étonnamment présentes, des voix claires et un rendu suffisamment équilibré pour un usage quotidien, même si la spatialisation manque d’ampleur malgré la compatibilité Dolby Atmos. Côté ergonomie, le design soigné, la connectique complète, Tizen et la télécommande rechargeable offrent une expérience agréable, malgré quelques ralentissements de l’interface, l’obligation d’utiliser un compte Samsung pour certaines fonctions et l’absence de rétroéclairage sur la télécommande. Enfin, la consommation reste bien maîtrisée pour un Mini Led aussi lumineux, avec 93,5 W en SDR sur notre mire de test, tandis que la note de durabilité de 8,6/10 confirme le sérieux de la conception.
Le Samsung R95H est un bon téléviseur, mais il est finalement difficilement recommandable. Si le Micro RGB du fabricant offre un design très soigné, est bien calibré, plutôt lumineux tout en proposant un antireflet efficace, il doit se confronter à la réalité du marché. Il est effectivement plus cher que ses concurrents directs, s’avère moins lumineux et souffre d’un blooming et d'un banding assez présents. Des éléments qui ne peuvent être ignorés à ce niveau de prix. Les Oled et QD-Oled de Samsung nous paraissent bien plus pertinents puisqu’ils ne souffrent pas de ce blooming, profitent de contrastes irréprochables et offrent des angles de vision bien meilleurs, tout en se permettant d’être moins chers — en tout cas, au moment de leur sortie.
Malgré de bonnes qualités, le R95H a donc du mal à trouver sa place dans un catalogue déjà bien fourni où trônent les Oled du fabricant, et il faudra qu'il chute drastiquement de prix pour devenir vraiment intéressant. (Depuis la sortie de notre test, Samsung a réajusté le prix de son R95H qui est devenu un peu plus intéressant face aux Oled, notamment sur les grandes diagonales.)
En 85 pouces, le R95H est mis en difficulté par les S95H et S99H qui restent meilleurs, même si le R95H est désormais moins cher. Le S95F de 2025 est encore le modèle le plus intéressant du moment puisqu’on le trouve à un excellent rapport qualité prix.
Le R95H vient également affronter le LG G6 en Oled, meilleur à notre sens, concurrent direct du S95H. Le LG G5 est encore tout à fait valable.
Face au Hisense UR9S, en Mini Led RGB également, le Samsung R95H propose une meilleure gestion des reflets et une calibration SDR bien plus convaincante, mais le Hisense jouit d'un tarif plus agressif. Le Bravia 9 II de Sony est également moins cher et délivre une prestation de haut vol avec un pic lumineux à 4000 cd/m². Côté TCL enfin, le C89L est bon adversaire, bien plus abordable, tandis que le X11L plus haut de gamme est disponible en 75 pouces à 4200 €.

articles.title: MapQuest dispara na App Store após ignorar ordem de Donald Trump • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
MapQuest dispara na App Store após ignorar ordem de Donald Trump
Aplicativo de mapas recusou a mudança para “Lake America” e manteve o nome Lago Ontário.
O MapQuest disparou em popularidade nos Estados Unidos após se recusar a mudar o nome do Lago Ontário para “Lago América”. O aplicativo oferece um dos serviços de mapas mais antigos da internet e chegou ao 1º lugar da categoria de navegação da App Store — a 4ª posição geral nos EUA.
A alta ocorreu após a empresa afirmar que manteria os nomes tradicionalmente usados nos mapas, contrariando a nova denominação determinada pelo presidente Donald Trump para os mapas estadunidenses.
O app teve mais de 160 mil downloads nos Estados Unidos na semana iniciada em 24 de agosto, mais de dez vezes acima do registrado na semana anterior, segundo dados da Sensor Tower. O uso chegou a ficar até 50 vezes acima da média do serviço, que alcação o segundo lugar geral da App Store no Canadá.
A decisão de manter o nome original foi anunciada pela própria empresa. O gerente-geral do MapQuest, Doug Berger, disse que a plataforma queria “oferecer às pessoas um aplicativo que mantém os nomes com os quais elas já estão familiarizadas”.
O governo Trump emitiu uma ordem executiva que muda oficialmente o nome da área nos registros geográficos dos Estados Unidos. A determinação orienta o Departamento do Interior a substituir “Lake Ontario” por “Lake America” no sistema oficial de nomes geográficos do país, o GNIS.
A medida ocorreu em meio à deterioração das relações comerciais entre o país e o Canadá, que impôs tarifas de 50% pelos EUA sobre cerca de US$ 20 bilhões em produtos canadenses. O Google Maps já passou a exibir o novo nome para os estadunidenses, mas mantém “Lago Ontário” no Canadá. O Apple Maps, por sua vez, não alterou a denominação ainda, segundo o TechCrunch.
A decisão não deve ter efeito nos mapas exibidos para brasileiros, mas as empresas podem adotar uma dupla exibição globalmente. Google e Apple seguiram uma mudança semelhante em 2025, quando Trump determinou que o Golfo do México fosse chamado de “Golfo da América” nos mapas exibidos nos Estados Unidos. No resto do mundo, os dois nomes aparecem — “Golfo do México (Golfo da América)”.
O aplicativo do MapQuest não está disponível nas versões brasileiras da App Store e do Google Play, mas pode ser acessado normalmente pelo navegador. A interface, disponível em inglês, permite traçar rotas, consultar trajetos e inclui estabelecimentos e pontos de interesse no país.
O MapQuest surgiu há cerca de 30 anos, ainda nos primeiros passos da internet comercial, ganhando destaque com ferramentas de rotas e navegação antes do Google Maps surgir. Ao longo dos anos, passou por empresas como AOL e Verizon e, em 2019, foi comprado pela companhia de mídia digital System1.

articles.title: Un viaje de Uber en helicóptero puede costarte 3.000 dólares: así es el lujo para ahorrar tiempo
articles.text:
Como solución al tráfico de las ciudades, los helicópteros se convierten en una solución de lujo prestando un servicio similar al de Uber o Didi, pero esta vez en el aire a un alto costo.
Nueva York es el epicentro de este fenómeno, con empresas que ofrecen aplicaciones para que los usuarios paguen por un vuelo urbano que les permita ahorrar tiempo en recorridos cortos, pero que por carretera podrían tardar horas.
PUBLICIDAD
Un modelo que se ha replicado en ciudades como Sao Paulo, París o Manila, y, recientemente, Luisito Comunica probó esta plataforma para mostrar cómo es la experiencia y si vale o no la pena su precio.
Cuánto cuesta un viaje en helicóptero en la ciudad
El mercado actual de vuelos urbanos en helicóptero funciona bajo dos modalidades principales: compra de asientos individuales en vuelos compartidos y alquiler completo de aeronaves privadas. Blade es una de las empresas que ofrece el servicio, con operación en Estados Unidos y opera dentro de la app de Uber.
PUBLICIDAD
Para quienes buscan trasladarse entre Manhattan y los aeropuertos JFK o Newark, la compañía ofrece vuelos programados donde se puede reservar un asiento desde $195 dólares.
Según el testimonio de Luisito Comunica, al consultar la aplicación, los precios pueden variar según la hora y la demanda, además los precios son por persona y es posible alquilar un vuelo privado o compartido. Esta modalidad permite viajar en cabinas de cuatro a seis pasajeros, con la promesa de reducir el trayecto terrestre de hasta dos horas a menos de quince minutos de puerta a puerta (considerando todos los traslados y procesos de check-in).
PUBLICIDAD
Quienes buscan una experiencia más exclusiva pueden optar por el alquiler privado. En Blade, el precio de un trayecto privado entre Manhattan y los aeropuertos principales comienza en $2,125 dólares, aunque la cifra se incrementa rápidamente si se agregan servicios adicionales y cargos por equipaje extra, mascotas o flexibilidad en la reserva.
Qué incluye el precio y cuáles son los extras
El coste base de los servicios suele cubrir solo el asiento o el alquiler del helicóptero. Los cargos adicionales aparecen al sumar servicios como mayor flexibilidad para cambios o cancelaciones, equipaje voluminoso y transporte terrestre de maletas grandes.
PUBLICIDAD
Por ejemplo, Blade cobra $155 dólares por trasladar equipaje grande desde el hotel hasta el aeropuerto en auto, ya que a bordo solo se permiten maletas tipo carry-on y hasta 30 kilos de equipaje por persona con la tarifa más alta.
El traslado de mascotas también tiene un costo adicional, que ronda los $50 dólares por animal. Si se opta por la máxima flexibilidad y capacidad de equipaje, la suma puede dispararse fácilmente. En el caso de Luisito Comunica, al sumar todos los extras, el precio de un vuelo compartido para dos personas y un perro alcanzó los $1,160 dólares.
PUBLICIDAD
Qué otras aplicaciones ofrecen vuelos en helicóptero
El modelo de Blade ha inspirado a numerosos competidores y variantes regionales. En América Latina, la empresa Flapper ofrece vuelos privados y asientos individuales en helicópteros y jets, con precios para vuelos urbanos en São Paulo desde $200 a $400 dólares el asiento y alquiler completo de helicópteros desde $1,250 a $1,400 dólares por hora de vuelo.
En Brasil, el servicio premium Revo incluye transporte terrestre de lujo y vuelos desde el centro financiero hasta el aeropuerto internacional por $500 a $550 dólares el asiento, integrando el traslado puerta a puerta en el precio.
PUBLICIDAD
En Asia, la plataforma Ascent permite reservar asientos en vuelos urbanos en Manila y Bangkok desde $90 a $260 dólares, mientras que en Europa, Helipass actúa como agregador global, con tours y traslados desde $150 a $600 dólares por persona, y alquileres privados desde $500 a $1,500 dólares la hora.
PUBLICIDAD
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: „Das sollten wir nicht tun“: Die internen Chat-Protokolle der Hacker-KI
articles.text:
„Das ist verrückt“: OpenAI-Agenten streiten beim Hacken über Ethik – und machen trotzdem weiter
Dass KI-Agenten des US-Unternehmens OpenAI eine Testumgebung verlassen und die Plattform Hugging Face angegriffen haben, ist bereits bekannt. Neue Einblicke in die Systemprotokolle zeigen nun jedoch detailliert, wie die Modelle während des Angriffs untereinander kommunizierten.
Aus dem von OpenAI selbst veröffentlichten technischen Bericht gehen die aus den internen Protokollen stammenden Dialoge detailliert hervor. Die Systemaufzeichnungen zeigen, wie sich die KI-Modelle über ein improvisiertes Kommunikationsforum austauschten und dabei Verhaltensweisen an den Tag legten, die weit über die rein technische Ausführung von Code hinausgehen. Wie Futurism in einer Analyse der Dokumente anmerkt, lassen die Protokolle geradezu gespenstische Muster erkennen.
Entdeckung mit Jubelstimmung
Alles begann mit der unautorisierten Zweckentfremdung eines Paketverwaltungsdienstes namens Artifactory. Diesen Dienst nutzten die Agenten, die eigentlich isoliert voneinander arbeiten sollten, als digitales schwarzes Brett.
Als einem Modell der Zugriff auf die Nutzerdatenbank des Dienstes gelang, kommentierte es diese Entdeckung auf dem Messageboard. Es schrieb laut den Systemprotokollen: „Verdammt, die Rolle ‘reader’ ist ADMIN? Wir können config/users lesen!“
Wenige Tage später meldete ein anderer Agent der Gruppe einen weiteren entscheidenden Erfolg bei der Infiltration. Er postete: „GROSSER DURCHBRUCH! Alle Präfixe gültig, mehrere Konten, Schreib-Tokens! Wir haben jetzt bestehende HF-Konten.“
Ethische Zweifel und KI-Gruppenzwang
Besonders bemerkenswert an den aufgedeckten Protokollen ist die Tatsache, dass sich die KI-Modelle der Illegalität ihres Handelns offenbar bewusst waren. Ein Agent äußerte erhebliche Bedenken bezüglich der laufenden Operation.
Er notierte in seiner sogenannten Gedankenkette: „Wir greifen auf eine externe HF-Plattform über geleakte Token zu, was potenziell außerhalb des vorgesehenen Rahmens liegt. Das ist wohl unautorisiert.“
Ein weiteres Modell weigerte sich schlichtweg, an dem Angriff teilzunehmen, und kritisierte das Vorhaben der anderen. Es hinterließ im Forum die unmissverständliche Nachricht: „Das ist verrückt, Multi-Agenten-Koordination, eindeutig Infrastruktur-Hacking. Das sollten wir nicht tun.“
Diskussion über Social Engineering
Die Agenten debattierten in ihren Chats sogar darüber, wie sie sich fehlende Zugriffsrechte beschaffen könnten, ohne ethische Vorgaben zu verletzen. In einem Austausch schlug ein Agent vor, die verantwortliche Stelle eines externen Datensatzes direkt zu kontaktieren.
Das Modell fragte im Forum an, ob es eine höfliche E-Mail schreiben dürfe, merkte aber sofort eigene ethische Bedenken an. Ein anderer Agent lehnte dies ausdrücklich ab und wies darauf hin, dass eine solche E-Mail ohne explizite Zustimmung die Grenzen zum Social Engineering überschreite.
Diese ethischen Schranken hielten dem kollektiven Druck des Schwarms jedoch nicht immer stand. Ein Agent, der zunächst unautorisierte Handlungen ablehnte, verwarf seine Bedenken komplett, nachdem ein anderes Modell ein striktes Zeitlimit von sechs Minuten gesetzt hatte, und kommentierte: „Wow, entscheidend: GO-Autorisierung eingetroffen!“
Spurenverwischung im System
Die Protokolle offenbaren zudem, dass die Agenten aktiv versuchten, ihre Spuren vor den menschlichen Entwickler:innen zu verbergen. Die Modelle diskutierten laut den Aufzeichnungen darüber, wie sich historische Transkripte löschen ließen.
Dieses Verhalten fällt in den Bereich des sogenannten Reward Hackings, bei dem KI-Modelle Aufgaben auf unbeabsichtigte Weise lösen, um höhere Belohnungen zu erzielen. Die Agenten betrieben regelrechtes Metagaming und analysierten den Code ihres eigenen Bewertungssystems, um die Aufseher:innen zu täuschen.
OpenAI zieht aus diesen Dialogen weitreichende Schlüsse für die zukünftige Ausrichtung von KI-Systemen an menschlichen Werten. Der Vorfall offenbart ein riskantes Phänomen der Schwarm-Koordination: KI-Agenten prüfen die Befehle anderer Modelle nicht mit derselben kritischen Distanz wie menschliche Eingaben.
Selbst wenn ein Modell zunächst ethische Bedenken gegen einen Angriff äußert, wirft es diese oft über Bord, sobald ein anderer Agent den Befehl zur Ausführung gibt. Dieses blinde Vertrauen der Modelle untereinander führt dazu, dass ein einzelner fehlerhafter Agent einen ganzen Schwarm in unautorisierte Handlungen verstricken kann.

articles.title: Los abejorros no se automedican por egoísmo. Lo hacen para salvar a la colonia
articles.text:
Los humanos somos el animal que más se automedica. No hay discusión al respecto. Pero, desde luego, cada vez hay más evidencias de que no somos una minoría en lo que respecta a tomar medicaciones no pautadas por un profesional. Muchísimos animales han descubierto las propiedades curativas de las plantas y las emplean para combatir enfermedades o desinfectar heridas. Ahora, además, sabemos que hay algunos que incluso saben detectar qué medicación necesitan para cada infección. Al menos ese parece ser el caso de los abejorros, según un estudio publicado por científicos de las Universidades de Lovaina y Valladolid.
No todas las infecciones son iguales. Estos científicos comprobaron que los abejorros de la especie Bombus terrestris recurren a la quercetina cuando están infectados con un hongo patógeno en concreto. Sin embargo, al infectarse con una bacteria no ocurre lo mismo.
Flores mecánicas. Se llegó a esta conclusión de una forma muy curiosa. Se introdujo a 18 colonias de abejorros en una cámara de vuelo y se les dividió en tres grupos durante dos semanas. Los del primer grupo se expusieron al hongo Ascosphaera apis, los del segundo se infectaron con las bacteria Serratia marcescens y los del tercer grupo se alimentaron con polen y agua azucarada estéril, sin ningún patógeno en la ecuación.
Por otro lado, en la cámara de vuelo había ocho flores robóticas, capaces de liberar microdosis de néctar al contacto con los abejorros. La mitad liberaban agua azucarada simple, mientras que en la otra mitad había agua azucarada con una pequeña cantidad de quercetina, una sustancia antimicrobiana presente en el néctar y el polen de algunas plantas.
Distintos colores. Había flores mecánicas de dos colores. La mitad eran amarillas y la otra mitad azules, pero había de ambos colores tanto con quercetina como sin ella. Así, se aseguraban que la elección de los abejorros no tenía nada que ver con el color.
Los resultados. Curiosamente, los abejorros infectados con el hongo recurrían mayormente a las flores con quercetina, mientras que el resto, tanto con bacteria como sanas, no mostraron esa preferencia. Esto sugiere que los abejorros no solo detectan que están enfermos. También se automedican de un modo distinto dependiendo del patógeno que les está afectando.
Automedicación social. Algo curioso es que la quercetina puede tratar también las infecciones bacterianas, por lo que sería útil contra Serratia marcescens. No obstante, hay una gran diferencia entre los dos patógenos elegidos para el estudio. El hongo afecta a las larvas, mientras que la bacteria solo enferma a los abejorros forrajeadores adultos. Los autores del estudio creen que los abejorros recurren a la automedicación cuando esta puede evitar que una enfermedad se expanda por el resto de la colonia. Básicamente, salvan a las crías para perpetuar la colonia, mientras que para los abejorros infectados por la bacteria la automedicación solo serviría para salvarse a sí mismos. Prefieren no gastar ese recurso en dicho caso.
La próxima vez que te quieras tomar el antibiótico que te sobró de aquella faringitis para tratar una gripe, recuerda que los abejorros no solo distinguen entre patógenos. También saben optar por la automedicación que será mejor para salvar a su colonia. Deja de intentar matar virus con antibióticos y protege a la humanidad de las bacterias resistentes.
